reports.title: TransDigm Group Reports Fiscal 2026 Fourth Quarter and Year-End Results

guidance.heading: Fiscal 2027 Outlook
section: Mr. Lisman stated, "We are issuing full year fiscal 2027 guidance today, which reflects our current expectations for the year. We are well-positioned for continued growth as we head into our fiscal 2027 across all three of our primary end markets."
TransDigm is issuing fiscal 2027 financial guidance to be as follows:
•Net sales are anticipated to be in the range of $11,950 million to $12,150 million compared with $10,557 million in fiscal 2026, an increase of 14% at the midpoint;
•Net income is anticipated to be in the range of $2,442 million to $2,490 million compared with $2,108 million in fiscal 2026, an increase of 17% at the midpoint;

•Earnings per share is expected to be in the range of $42.06 to $42.91 per share based upon weighted average shares outstanding of 56.7 million shares, compared with $35.51 per share in fiscal 2026, which is an increase of 20% at the midpoint;

•EBITDA As Defined is anticipated to be in the range of $6,195 million to $6,345 million compared with $5,563 million in fiscal 2026, an increase of 13% at the midpoint (corresponding to an EBITDA As Defined margin guide of approximately 52.0% for fiscal 2027);
•Adjusted earnings per share is expected to be in the range of $47.09 to $47.94 per share compared with $41.35 per share in fiscal 2026, an increase of 15% at the midpoint compared to prior year; and
•Fiscal 2027 outlook is based on the following market growth assumptions:
◦Commercial OEM revenue growth in the high single-digit to low double-digit percentage range;
◦Commercial aftermarket revenue growth in the high single-digit percentage range; and
◦Defense revenue growth in the high single-digit percentage range.

desk.headline: Revenue up 23% to $3.0bn and adjusted EPS of $12.44, both beat; first fiscal 2027 outlook points to 14% sales growth
results: Net sales rose 23% to $3.0bn, with 14% coming from existing businesses and the rest from acquisitions; adjusted EPS rose 15% to $12.44.
Net income slipped 4% to $586m because higher debt pushed interest costs up to $536m and the tax bill rose.
The EBITDA As Defined margin was 53.0%, down from 54.2%, with about two points of dilution from recently bought businesses.
Fiscal 2026 sales grew 20% to $10.56bn; about $4.4bn went on acquisitions (including Prince & Izant for about $1.07bn) and a record $2.8bn on buybacks.
Long-term debt rose to $33.7bn from $29.2bn a year earlier; $3.0bn of new 2035 notes were used mainly to refinance 2028 notes.

guidance.summary: TransDigm gave its first fiscal 2027 outlook: sales of $11.95–12.15bn (about 14% growth at the midpoint) and adjusted EPS of $47.09–47.94, with a margin of about 52%. It assumes high single-digit growth in the aftermarket and defense and high single- to low double-digit growth in OEM sales.

points: Commercial aftermarket sales grew about 17% in Q4, with bookings ahead of sales for the year; management expects high single-digit aftermarket growth in fiscal 2027.
Air traffic has come in below forecasts amid high oil prices and Middle East tension, but management said aftermarket orders have not yet been hurt much and called it a short-term dip.
Commercial OEM sales rose about 15%, helped by higher Boeing and Airbus build rates; defense grew about 12% in Q4, a third straight double-digit quarter.
Management said it has more than $10bn of capacity for deals, focused on small and mid-sized aerospace and defense targets, and favours buybacks when returns look attractive.
The finance chief put net debt at 5.9 times EBITDA and expects it below 5 times by the end of fiscal 2027, with free cash flow of about $2.9bn.
